doc.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Rehearsing with the Miles Davis Nonet before leaving
summary: Bert rehearsed with the Nonet; years later learned he was replaced after being called out of tune.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: It definitely was a — you had to grab the opportunities when they came, didn’t you?

Yeah. Well I went back to New York after we did the three weeks in Chicago and there was Nola Studios, which was the place to meet. And everybody rehearsed there and so I rehearsed with the Nonet with Miles Davis for four times. It was a good group. I enjoyed it and all that. I came in one day and Kai Winding was there so I said ahh, see you later. So I went down the hall and auditioned for Benny Goodman and I went with the bebop band.
You know, with Wardell Gray and them. Because they were right in the same place, you know, Nola’s. But you know Junior Collins that played with the Nonet? French horn?

About 20 years later I saw him on the street and he said, “hey I ever tell you what I told Miles you said?” I said, “no, what’d you tell him I said?” He said, “I told him you said the band was out of tune.” So 20 years later you find out why you were replaced.
So I said, “what’d you do that for?” He said, “ahh it was getting boring.”
